> **What this case shows** — the EEG power spectrum is not just its oscillatory
> peaks: beneath them lies an **aperiodic 1/f background** whose slope, the
> **aperiodic exponent**, has become a widely-used marker of cortical
> excitation/inhibition balance and state (Donoghue et al. 2020). The question is
> whether the ecosystem's parameterization of that background is trustworthy.
> Running `eegAperiodic` (the specparam engine) on all **64 channels** of a real
> eyes-closed resting EEG and comparing, channel by channel, against the canonical
> Python **fooof** shows they agree strongly: the per-channel exponents correlate
> **r = 0.98**, with a mean absolute difference of just **0.07**, and both engines
> return physiologically plausible resting exponents (specparam **1.38**, fooof
> **1.45**; mean fit **R² = 0.93**). **The ecosystem reproduces the field-standard
> tool — so its aperiodic exponent is a validated qEEG biomarker, not a bespoke
> number.**

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — to parameterize the spectrum: read the EEG → call
`eegAperiodic(pe, freq_range, aperiodic_mode)` → read the per-channel **exponent**
(the 1/f slope), **offset**, and the separated oscillatory **peaks** → map the
exponent as a qEEG biomarker (topomap, group contrast).
**Way of thinking** — never read a "band power" without accounting for the 1/f
background: a change in the aperiodic slope shifts *every* band. specparam / FOOOF
separates the genuine oscillations from the 1/f, so the exponent and the peaks are
each interpretable on their own.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioEEG::eegAperiodic()` (EEG-facing) wraps
`PhysioAnalysis::specparam()` (the engine); pair with `eegComplexity()` for
time-domain complexity and `bandPower()` for the oscillatory bands.
:::

## Proposition

On all 64 channels of a real eyes-closed resting EEG (eegmmidb S001R02),
`eegAperiodic` reproduces the canonical Python fooof: the per-channel aperiodic
exponents correlate r = 0.98, mean |diff| = 0.07, both means ~1.4 (mean R² = 0.93).

## Question & goal

**The question is whether the ecosystem's 1/f estimate is the field-standard
estimate.** The aperiodic exponent is only useful as a biomarker if it is
*comparable* — if the number the ecosystem reports is the number fooof would
report. The goal is a channel-by-channel head-to-head on real data, feeding the
*identical* power spectrum to both engines so any difference is the algorithm, not
the input.

## Challenge & approach

Two independent implementations of the same FOOOF model can drift — they fit the 1/f
iteratively and remove oscillatory peaks with slightly different heuristics. So we
compute the Welch PSD once, hand the *same* spectrum to `eegAperiodic` (specparam)
and to fooof with matched settings, and compare the per-channel exponents.

```
readEDF → eegAperiodic (specparam, per channel) ┐
                                                ├─ compare exponents → r, mean|diff|
same Welch PSD → fooof (Python, matched)        ┘
```

## Data

**eegmmidb — EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (PhysioNet)**: subject S001,
baseline run **R02 (eyes-closed rest)**, all 64 channels, 160 Hz, ~61 s — the
canonical resting condition for a 1/f analysis. The same EDF the sibling
`eeg-alpha` / `eeg-berger` cases read. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: the aperiodic exponent for each of the 64 channels — eegAperiodic (specparam) versus the canonical fooof, on the dashed identity line (r = 0.98, mean |diff| = 0.07). Right: the per-channel absolute difference, sorted; only 4 of 64 channels (occipital, plus one temporal edge) exceed 0.15 (red), where a strong alpha peak makes the two peak-removal heuristics diverge.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* if the ecosystem reproduced fooof exactly, every point on the
left would sit on the dashed line. They cluster tightly along it (r = 0.98); the
spread on the right is small and concentrated at the occipital electrodes.

| Quantity | This reproduction | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Exponent correlation (64 ch) | **0.98** | fooof (Python) |
| Mean \|exponent diff\| | **0.070** | — |
| Mean exponent | **1.38** (specparam) | **1.45** (fooof) |
| Mean fit R² | **0.93** | — |

The two engines agree strongly across the head, with a small systematic offset
(specparam slightly below fooof) and the largest divergence at the occipital
electrodes. Values trace to
[`artifacts/eeg_aperiodic_summary.csv`](artifacts/eeg_aperiodic_summary.csv) and the
per-channel table
[`artifacts/eeg_aperiodic_by_channel.csv`](artifacts/eeg_aperiodic_by_channel.csv).

## Conclusion

The ecosystem's aperiodic parameterization reproduces the field-standard fooof on
real resting EEG — so the aperiodic exponent it reports is a *validated* qEEG
biomarker. The transferable takeaway: **separate the 1/f background before you read
the spectrum, and use an estimator you have checked against the canonical tool — the
exponent is only a biomarker if it is comparable.**

## Open questions

- The occipital divergence traces to peak-model differences under a strong alpha
  rhythm; a **knee-mode** fit, a broader peak-width prior, or matched peak-removal
  settings would likely tighten the agreement there. Extending to multi-subject
  **test-retest** (is the exponent a stable trait?), an **eyes-open vs eyes-closed**
  contrast (does it track arousal?), and a clinical group difference would turn a
  validated estimator into a qEEG biomarker study. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| aperiodic (1/f) parameterization | `eegAperiodic()` | PhysioEEG |
| the specparam engine (any signal) | `specparam()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| band power (oscillatory bands) | `bandPower()` | PhysioEEG |
| time-domain complexity | `eegComplexity()` | PhysioEEG |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **freq_range** — fit over a range that captures the 1/f without edge artefacts
  (here 1–40 Hz); avoid the line-noise band.
- **aperiodic_mode** — `"fixed"` for a straight 1/f in log-log; `"knee"` when the
  spectrum bends (broadband or long recordings).
- **peak settings** — `max_n_peaks` / `peak_width_limits` control how oscillations
  are separated from the background; mismatched peak settings are the usual source
  of exponent disagreement (see the occipital channels here).

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioEEG)

pe <- readEDF("S001R02.edf")                       # 64-ch eyes-closed rest
ap <- eegAperiodic(pe, freq_range = c(1, 40), aperiodic_mode = "fixed")
ap$aperiodic$exponent                              # per-channel 1/f slope (biomarker)
mean(ap$aperiodic$exponent)                         # 1.38  (fooof: 1.45)
mean(ap$aperiodic$r_squared)                        # 0.93  (fit quality)
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/`](artifacts/) — the summary in
[`eeg_aperiodic_summary.csv`](artifacts/eeg_aperiodic_summary.csv) and the
per-channel exponents in

[`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks each reported number, the fooof agreement, the fit
quality, and the honestly-reported occipital divergence.
